text:
The only failing spec is power (999 µW vs. 400 µW max). Gain, bandwidth, and offset all pass, so the fault is most likely in the output-stage bias.

Total current is about 555 µA × 1.8 V ≈ 1 mW, and almost all of it is the output-stage sink M8 at 518 µA. M8 mirrors M6 (10 µA) at roughly 52×. The sizing ratio is (7.5 × 3 / 0.49) ≈ 46×, which matches once the small Vds difference is accounted for. The +20% sensitivities agree: M8 +20.6% and M6 −16.9% are both mirror-ratio effects. M5 barely matters (+0.85%), so the triode tail is not the cause of the power violation.

Dropping M8 from m=3 to m=1 would give a ratio of about 15× and roughly 150 µA in the output stage. Total power would then be about 340 µW, under the limit. The first-stage gm and Cc are unchanged, so bandwidth should stay well above 260 MHz.
